Offline CI consumers use the approved private `DOCSPEC_RUNTIME_ARTIFACT` binary with a credential-free local job configuration. The shared action preserves F1's installation order, reuses `setup-native-runtime.py --local`, checks exact binary bytes and application source pins, applies `.github/docspec-local-limits.json`, then runs `scripts/dev.py doctor --lane production-offline` before exporting `DOCSPEC_JOB_CONFIG`, `DOCSPEC_BINARY` and its SHA-256.

`DOCSPEC_ENGINE_CREDENTIALS` is supplied only to the installation step to read the private runtime bucket. Local mode never reads the remote configuration or writes credentials/remote files; neither is present in the exported job config. Trusted validation keeps the existing same-repository pull-request boundary. Missing credentials, an unapproved source, invalid limits, changed binary, stale destination or failed doctor stops before the offline consumers. The account ID reuses the existing public workflow configuration, so no new repository variable is required.

The ordinary runtime is built with `remote`, without `test-util`. The six committed local limits use four compute threads, 14 GiB pool memory, 6 GiB scratch, 8,192 batch rows, 64 MiB batch bytes and 32 MiB metadata bytes. These are explicit CI ceilings; source admission and runtime tests enforce them. They are not a full-corpus memory qualification.

The former public archive installer remains intact for its existing packaging callers until legacy cleanup. CI no longer needs `DOCSPEC_LOCAL_RUNTIME_URL` or `DOCSPEC_LOCAL_RUNTIME_SHA256`. The lead uploads the tested private binary and sets `DOCSPEC_RUNTIME_ARTIFACT`; release performs no upload, variable write or hosted run.
